question.text: Given that $f(x,y)=\arctan \left(\dfrac{x}{y} \right),$ find the set of values $(x,y)$ on which $\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y}$ exists.
question.explanation:
First, notice that $f(x,y)$ is not defined when $y=0.$ So, the domain of $f$ is \[ D_f = \{(x,y) \, : \, y\ne 0 \}. \]

Now, we compute the partial derivatives of $f(x,y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_y(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial} {\partial y}\left(\arctan \left(\dfrac{x}{y} \right)\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-\dfrac{x}{y^2}}{1 + \left(\dfrac{x}{y} \right)^2} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{x}{y^2 +x^2} \end{align*}

The function $f_y(x,y)$ is not defined at the point $(0,0).$ So, the domain of $f_y$ is

\[ D_{f_y} = \big\{ (x,y) \,:\, x^2+y^2 \neq 0 \big\}. \]

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ exists on the set

\begin{align*} D_f \cap D_{f_y} &= \big\{ (x,y) \,:\, y \neq 0 \big\} \cap \big\{ (x,y) \,:\, x^2+y^2 \neq 0 \big\} \\[3pt] &= \big\{ (x,y) \,:\, y \neq 0 \big\}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{xy-z},$ find the set of values $(x,y,z)$ on which $\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y}$ exists.
question.explanation:
First, notice that $f(x,y,z)$ is defined only when

\begin{align*} xy-z &\geq 0 \\[3pt] xy &\geq z. \end{align*}

So, the domain of $f$ is \[ D_f = \{(x,y,z) \, : \, xy \geq z \}. \]

Now, we compute the partial derivative of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_y(x,y,z) &= \dfrac {\partial} {\partial y}\left(\sqrt{ xy - z}\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{xy -z}} \cdot x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x}{2\sqrt{xy-z}} \end{align*}

The function $f_y(x,y,z)$ is defined only for

\begin{align*} xy -z & > 0 \\[3pt] xy &> z. \end{align*}

So, the domain of $f_y$ is

\[ D_{f_y} = \big\{ (x,y,z) \,:\, xy > z \big\}. \]

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ exists on the set

\begin{align*} D_f \cap D_{f_y} &= \{(x,y,z) \, : \, xy \geq z \} \cap \big\{ (x,y,z) \,:\, xy >z \big\} \\[3pt] &=\big\{ (x,y,z) \,:\, xy > z \big\}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Domain Where a Partial Derivative Exists

question.text: Given that $h(x,y)=\arccos(xy)$ and \[ \dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} =-\dfrac{y}{\sqrt{1 - (xy)^2}}, \qquad \dfrac{\partial h}{\partial y} =-\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - (xy)^2}}, \] find the set of values $(x,y)$ on which all partial derivatives of $h$ exist.
question.explanation:
First, notice that $h(x,y)=\arccos(xy)$ is defined only when $-1 \leq xy \leq 1.$ So, the domain of $h$ is \[ D_h = \{(x,y) \, : \, -1 \leq xy \leq 1 \}. \]

As for the partial derivatives, we have the following.

  • The function $\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} =-\dfrac{y}{\sqrt{1 - (xy)^2}}$ is defined only when \begin{align*} 1 - (xy)^2 & > 0 \\[3pt] (xy)^2 & < 1 \\[3pt] |xy| & < 1, \end{align*} which gives $-1 < xy < 1.$ So, the domain of $h_x$ is \[ D_{h_x} = \{(x,y) \, : \, -1 < xy < 1 \}. \]

  • Similarly, the domains of $h_y$ is the same: \[ D_{h_y} = \{(x,y) \, : \, -1 < xy < 1 \}. \]

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivatives of $h$ exist on the set

\begin{align*} D_h \cap D_{h_x} \cap D_{h_y} &= D_h \cap D_{h_x} \\[3pt] &= \{(x,y) \, : \, -1 \leq xy \leq 1 \} \cap \{(x,y) \, : \, -1 < xy < 1 \} \\[3pt] &= \{(x,y) \, : \, -1 < xy < 1 \}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that $f(x,y,z)=\dfrac{z}{\sqrt{x-y}},$ find the set of values $(x,y,z)$ on which $\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y}$ exists.
question.explanation:
First, notice that $f(x,y,z)$ is defined only when \begin{align*} x-y &\gt 0. \end{align*}

So, the domain of $f$ is \[ D_f = \{(x,y,z) \, : \, x-y \gt 0 \}. \]

Now, we compute the partial derivative of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_y(x,y,z) &= \dfrac {\partial} {\partial y}\left(\dfrac{z}{\sqrt{x-y}}\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{z}{2\sqrt{(x-y)^3}} \end{align*}

The function $f_y(x,y,z)$ is defined only for

\begin{align*} x-y \gt 0. \end{align*}

So, the domain of $f_y$ is

\[ D_{f_y} = \big\{ (x,y,z) \,:\, x-y > 0 \big\}. \]

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ exists on the set

\begin{align*} D_f \cap D_{f_y} &= \{(x,y,z) \, : \, x-y \gt 0 \} \cap \big\{ (x,y,z) \,:\, x-y > 0\big\} \\[5pt] &=\big\{ (x,y,z) \,:\, x-y > 0\big\}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that $f(x,y,z)=\dfrac{\ln(x+z)}{y},$ find the set of values $(x,y,z)$ on which $\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial z}$ exists.
question.explanation:
First, notice that $f(x,y,z)$ is defined only when

\begin{align*} x+z &\gt 0 \quad \text{and} \quad y \neq 0 \end{align*}

So, the domain of $f$ is \[ D_f = \big\{(x,y,z) \, : \, x+z \gt 0 \,\, \text{and} \,\, y \neq 0 \big\}. \]

Now, we compute the partial derivative of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} f_z(x,y,z) &= \dfrac {\partial} {\partial z}\left(\dfrac{\ln(x+z)}{y}\right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{y} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x+z} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{y(x+z)} \end{align}

The function $f_z(x,y,z)$ is defined only for

\begin{align*} x+z & \ne 0 \quad \text{and} \quad y \neq 0 \end{align*}

So, the domain of $f_z$ is

\[ D_{f_z} = \big\{ (x,y,z) \,:\, x+z \ne 0 \,\, \text{and} \,\, y \neq 0 \big\}. \]

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $z$ exists on the set

\begin{align*} D_f \cap D_{f_z} &= \big\{(x,y,z) \, : \, x+z \gt 0 \,\, \text{and} \,\, y \neq 0 \big\} \cap \big\{ (x,y,z) \,:\, x+z \ne 0 \,\, \text{and} \,\, y \neq 0 \big\} \\[5pt] &=\big\{ (x,y,z) \,:\, x+z \gt 0 \,\, \text{and} \,\, y \neq 0 \big\}. \end{align*}
